# Section 6: Faculty

Section 6 addresses faculty qualifications, governance, and professional development.

## Standard 6.1 — Full-time Faculty [CR] {.core-requirement}

::: {.callout-important}
## Core Requirement
:::

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution employs an adequate number of full-time faculty to support its mission and programs.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Faculty roster with full-time/part-time status
- Full-time faculty count by program/department
- Student-to-faculty ratios
- Analysis demonstrating adequacy

### Suggested Owners

- Chief Academic Officer
- Department Chairs / Program Directors

### Common Pitfalls / Weak Evidence

- High reliance on part-time faculty without justification
- Insufficient full-time faculty in certain programs
- No clear methodology for determining adequacy

::: {.callout-note title="NC Considerations"}
NC community colleges operate under SBCC policies regarding faculty staffing. Reference:

- SBCC requirements for faculty ratios
- State funding model implications
- Curriculum vs. continuing education distinctions
:::

---

## Standards 6.2.a-c — Faculty Qualifications

### Standard 6.2.a — Credentials

**What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure:** Faculty teaching credit-bearing courses have appropriate academic credentials.

**Key Requirements:**

- **General Education:** Master's degree with 18 graduate semester hours in the discipline
- **Associate-level Career/Technical:** Bachelor's degree in the field OR associate's plus demonstrated competencies
- **Baccalaureate (if applicable):** Terminal degree or master's plus 18 graduate hours in discipline

### Standard 6.2.b — Graduate Teaching Assistants

**What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure:** Graduate teaching assistants (if used) have appropriate preparation and supervision.

*Note: Most community colleges do not use graduate teaching assistants. If your institution does not, state this clearly.*

### Standard 6.2.c — Non-Degree Credential Instructors

**What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure:** Instructors in non-degree programs have appropriate credentials or demonstrated competence.

### Typical Evidence Types for 6.2

- Faculty roster with credentials for each course assignment
- Transcripts on file for all faculty
- Credential matrix showing qualifications
- Alternative qualification justifications where needed
- Supervision documentation for any GTAs

### Common Pitfalls / Weak Evidence

- Missing transcripts
- Faculty teaching outside credentialed areas
- Insufficient alternative qualification documentation
- No credential verification process

---

## Standard 6.3 — Faculty Appointment and Evaluation

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Policies and procedures for faculty appointment and evaluation are published and consistently applied.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Faculty handbook sections on appointment
- Evaluation policies and forms
- Completed evaluation examples (redacted)
- Board policies on faculty

---

## Standard 6.4 — Academic Freedom

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution publishes and follows a policy on academic freedom.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Academic freedom policy
- Faculty handbook references
- Board policy approval

---

## Standard 6.5 — Faculty Development

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution provides ongoing professional development for faculty.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Professional development policies
- Funding allocations for development
- Development program descriptions
- Participation records

::: {.callout-note title="NC Considerations"}
NC community colleges have access to System-level professional development through the NC Community College System Office. Document both:

- Local professional development programs
- System-level opportunities utilized
:::

---

## Reflective Prompts

- How do we ensure all faculty meet credential requirements before teaching?
- What is our process for addressing credential gaps?
- How do we balance full-time and part-time faculty appropriately?
